title: Variation of Parameters
short: A general method for any forcing term.

blocks.html: Undetermined coefficients needs forcing terms whose derivatives stay in a small family. For $\sec t$, $\ln t$ or $\frac{1}{t}$ there is no finite guess. Variation of parameters works for any continuous $g$, as long as you know two independent homogeneous solutions.
For $y'' + p(t)y' + q(t)y$ $= g(t)$ (standard form) with homogeneous solutions $y_1, y_2$ and Wronskian $W$: $$y_p = u_1y_1 + u_2y_2,$$ $$u_1' = -\frac{y_2\,g}{W},$$ $$u_2' = \frac{y_1\,g}{W}.$$

Replace the constants in $c_1y_1 + c_2y_2$ by functions: $y_p = u_1y_1 + u_2y_2$. We may impose one extra condition, and we choose $u_1'y_1 + u_2'y_2 = 0$ so that $y_p' = u_1y_1' + u_2y_2'$ has no $u'$ terms. Then $y_p''$ $= u_1'y_1' + u_2'y_2' + u_1y_1''$ $+ u_2y_2''$. Substituting, the $u_1$ and $u_2$ terms cancel (each $y_i$ solves the homogeneous equation), leaving $u_1'y_1' + u_2'y_2' = g$. Solving these two linear equations by Cramer's rule gives the formulas, with $W$ as the determinant.

blocks.title: A secant forcing
blocks.q: Find $y_p$ for $y'' + y = \sec t$ on $-\frac{\pi}{2} < t < \frac{\pi}{2}$.

blocks.title: A repeated root and $\frac{1}{t}$
steps: $-te^{t}$ is a homogeneous solution, so it can be dropped.

blocks.title: Standard form matters
steps: Divide by $t^{2}$: the forcing in standard form is $g = t$, not $t^{3}$.

blocks.html: Using the original right side instead of the standard-form $g$; the formulas assume the coefficient of $y''$ is 1. Another slip is swapping $y_1$ and $y_2$ in one formula but not the other, which flips a sign. Check by substituting $y_p$ into the equation.
